s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: elevated troponin and inflammatory markers with normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: chest pain with radiation to the jaw and ST-segment elevations on ECG

shortlist.label: acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: chest pressure and elevated troponin, although coronary angiography was normal

shortlist.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: transient chest pressure and elevated troponin with normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: elevated troponin and chest pain, although coronary angiography showed no occlusions

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein), and ECG findings (ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression) are consistent with pericarditis. The normal coronary angiography and transthoracic echocardiogram results also support this diagnosis, as they rule out other cardiac conditions such as myocardial infarction or structural heart disease.

rejected.label: myocarditis
rejected.why: While myocarditis could explain the elevated troponin level, the normal cardiac examination and echocardiogram results make it less likely.

rejected.label: acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The normal coronary angiography results rule out this diagnosis.

rejected.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiogram and the presence of pericarditic ECG changes make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary angiography results and the lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiogram rule out this diagnosis.
